california.caveats: Transit stops are from today's map, not a pre-2023 one; and the comparison ring itself rose against land farther away, which could pull the estimate down. Analysis by the transit-oriented density work (docs/tod/AB2097_TEST_RESULTS.md).
california.text: California's AB 2097 removed parking minimums within half a mile of major transit stops from 1 January 2023. Comparing permits near transit with permits half a mile to a mile and a half away, in jurisdictions that had not already removed minimums or raised density near transit, gives the same answer as the city repeals: no measurable change in 2023–2025.

developer_parking: Assumption about parking developers build without mandates: developers keep building the parking that renters, buyers and lenders want, so a repeal adds homes only where a minimum forced more parking than the market wanted. In Buffalo after its 2017 repeal, major projects provided 79% of the old minimum (mixed-use 47%; stand-alone apartments 117%). In Los Angeles projects that could cut parking, five that list their unit mix built 67% of the old requirement. The scenario sets no parking ratio itself: it uses the permit outcomes of places that repealed, so whatever parking their developers chose is already built in.
north_carolina: North Carolina's HB 162, signed 6 July 2026, removes minimum parking for new projects statewide from 1 January 2027 (the 20 coastal counties are exempt). It is the closest real law to this scenario; it has no permit data yet.

places.evidence: The draft ordinance (council item 11-29-2022) removes minimums in Ch. 20.90 and in downtown 20.70, keeping a new 20.90.800 minimum only for office uses near the arena and Google DA area, and adds a TDM Part 9 for larger projects. City page gives in-effect date of April 10, 2023 (PRN said March 2023).
Ordinance 20231102-028 removed motor-vehicle parking minimums citywide for all uses; a city document says it took effect 2023-11-13. HOME housing-capacity reforms followed within weeks.

Board of Supervisors passed the ordinance 7-4 on Dec 11, 2018; Mayor signed Dec 21, 2018; it removed all remaining minimums for all uses including residential (sources give effective Jan 20 or Jan 21, 2019). Primary ordinance PDF could not be read.

City says the 2040 General Plan (adopted 2024-02-27, effective 2024-03-28) ended minimum vehicle parking for all properties; a Title 17 cleanup ordinance was still in progress in 2025-2026. Big simultaneous upzoning (FAR, missing middle) confounds timing.

City project page says TC-11-21 removes minimum vehicle parking requirements wherever they apply and adds parking maximums and bike parking; council approved it 7-1 on March 15, 2022. Effective date not found.
City 2040 implementation page says council adopted the parking/loading/TDM overhaul on May 14, 2021, eliminating minimum off-street parking citywide; published ordinance in effect May 22, 2021.

Legistar record shows Ordinance O-113-2022 (PLN-ZOTA-22-00014), approved Oct 27, 2022, consolidating parking rules into Article 16 and eliminating minimum parking requirements. Current code text and effective date not checked.
City parking-study page says Ordinance 21-27, adopted Aug 18, 2021 and effective Oct 1, 2021, eliminated minimum parking regulations citywide; TDM applies to larger projects.
City SCAD analysis says the amendment removes all minimum parking rate requirements; council approved 2023-11-20. Effective date not found.

AO 2022-80(S) text says off-street parking spaces are not required except ADA, loading and bike spaces, and takes effect 60 days after passage; Assembly passed it unanimously Nov 22, 2022. Effective date computed as 60 days after passage (PRN says Jan 22, 2023).

Secondary sources say the Green Code, adopted at end of 2016 and effective Jan 2017, has no minimum parking for any use, with a TDM plan required for larger projects. Rated near because large projects go through TDM review. City UDO PDF could not be downloaded; exact adoption date not confirmed (effective date is from PRN).
City planning page: council adopted ordinance eliminating off-street parking minimums on 2023-04-24 (reported as Ord. 2023-101). Citywide ADU legalization followed five months later.
Council passed Right Size Parking ordinance 6-0 on 2024-05-07 replacing minimums with maximums citywide. One TV report saying downtown is unaffected reflects that downtown already had no minimums.
Council voted unanimously 2024-10-22 to eliminate off-street minimum parking citywide (news report). Ordinance text and effective date not read directly.

City says council adopted code changes eliminating minimum off-street parking citywide (2023-11-13); reports say effective start of 2024. Large share of city was already exempt near transit since end of 2022.
City notice of decision says Ordinance Bill 4-23, adopted 2023-04-24, removes citywide minimum off-street parking mandates. PRN's 2023-04-10 is likely first reading; effective date not found.

Planning and Zoning Commission minutes from June 30, 2025 show the petition to restore residential parking minimums under section 8.20.1 failed (4 votes, needed 5) and was denied. Original 2021 adoption is from PRN; current code text not read. Watch for later attempts.

News reports say the commission removed minimum parking for new development in 2022 (Ordinance 211262 per PRN), keeping maximums and a structured-parking rule for big lots. The single-family zoning repeal passed the same autumn and was reversed in 2023, which overlaps with the parking repeal. Municode text not read.

City approval notice says ORD-22-13, adopted Aug 15, 2022, eliminates minimum vehicle parking citywide and takes effect 10 days after publication on Aug 25, 2022 (effective date calculated from that).
Streetsblog reports the Planning & Zoning Commission voted unanimously on about Dec 12, 2017 to remove parking minimums citywide, after a 2016 first phase. No PRN citation; city code not read.

Code table shows 'None required' for dwellings everywhere except narrow Hillside Overlay roads; council approved the change in a late-January 2021 vote (date from news; second reading/effective date not found).
Petition (Ordinance 2022-5) sets minimum accessory parking at 0 spaces for all uses in all districts in section 6.36, including single-family and multifamily. Council approved it 8-1 on Oct 24, 2022.
Council voted 4-2 on 2023-01-18; city notice says Ordinance NS-2462 took effect 2023-03-03 and code no longer requires on-site parking.

Greater Ohio reports the council voted in January 2021 to end parking minimums for commercial and residential development citywide; APA summary of the code says no off-street parking is required for any use. Ordinance number, exact date and effective date not found in primary records.
places.place: South Bend (with unincorporated St. Joseph County)

places.evidence: Council voted unanimously in late May 2024 (2024-05-28 per agenda) to drop minimums and set maximums. Ordinance number/effective date not read.

The Nov-2021 amendment redline changes 'Minimum parking requirement applies' from Yes to No in every residential district (RA through RMF), and in other districts as well. Code history cites Ord. 42205 of 11-15-21. PRN gives Nov 1, 2021, but the code history points to Nov 15, 2021.
Council minutes: Ordinance 4844 (TA 2023-0001) adopted 7-0 on 2023-07-18; staff report says it removes all minimum off-street parking citywide. Effective date not found.

New LDO (Ord. 23-70, adopted 2023-12-21) says off-street parking is not required, but TDM plans for 10+ unit housing can impose parking at site plan review. Repeal is bundled with a full code rewrite.

Ordinance 10868 (2023-12-11) removed zoning (UDC) parking minimums; companion ordinance 23-049-O kept rental-license parking requirements unchanged. Effective 30 days after publication (exact date not found).

The current UDO section 10.12 has only a 'Maximum Vehicle Parking' table plus minimum bicycle parking (Ord. 23-787, 6-20-23). The city amendment list shows an Aug 10, 2021 ordinance (21-742) clarifying 'recently revised parking standards', so the original repeal predates it. I could not find the exact adoption date, and PRN's 2021-08-18 is unverified.

The ordinance replaces AMC 30-7 and says no off-street vehicle parking is required for any use, including residential. It was on the Nov 16, 2021 agenda for final passage and takes effect 30 days later, which matches PRN's Dec 16, 2021.
Zoning Article 7 says there is no minimum vehicle parking except as noted; table keeps a 1-per-unit minimum for off-campus student housing. Adopted with the 2023-10-16 zoning code/map update.

Ordinance 24-34 (passed 2024-07-23 with emergency clause) adopted the new UDC, which PRN cites for no minimums; I did not read the UDC parking section directly. Repeal is bundled with a full code rewrite.
Council unanimously adopted ReCode on 2024-11-04; city housing update says it took effect 2024-12-04. Repeal is bundled with major upzoning.
Ordinance 6465 (final reading 2023-11-20) says no minimum motor vehicle parking is required; city says effective 2024-01-08.

Special Ordinance 2022-28 repeals all parking mandates within city limits and directs the City Manager not to enforce them (passed 11/21/2022, effective 12/31/2022). Ord. 2023-19 then re-enacted LDC 4.1, saying a minimum number of off-street spaces is not required.

WAMC 19.44 sets only 'Motor Vehicle Parking Limits' (maximums) plus bicycle minimums, with history 'Adopted by Ord. O-2022-0024 on 5/3/2022'. The parking change came bundled with a full zoning code replacement.
City CFEC page says effective 2023-07-01 the city no longer requires parking for any development; council hearing 2023-05-24 and adoption 2023-06-14 (adoption date from PRN/agenda).

Council unanimously adopted Ord. No. 22-10 on 12/13/2022, removing minimum parking citywide. Code 18.410 now lists vehicle maximums and bicycle minimums only. The effective date was reported as January 2023 (30 days later), but I did not confirm the exact date.

The council packet ordinance converts every Sec. 27-202 vehicle minimum to a maximum citywide. First reading was July 8, 2019 and second reading was on the July 22, 2019 agenda, but I did not see the final vote. PRN's 2019-01-01 looks like a placeholder.

Ordinance 5317 (file 24-1323), adopted by Common Council 9-3 on 2024-12-12, repealed and recreated Sec. 115-393 to remove all off-street parking requirements, including residential. Effective (publication) date not found.

ZA-22-07 (Ordinance 8.04) adopted 2023-01-09 (10-1), signed 2023-01-17, effective 2023-02-15, eliminates minimums in all parking districts for all uses. The only remaining minimum is for over-occupancy (more than 4 unrelated adults) applications.

Code 17.320.020 (Ord. 2022-008) says there is no minimum required parking for any use. Council voted 3-2 on Oct 24, 2022. The effective date is not confirmed (California ordinances usually take effect 30 days after adoption).
Article 25 (revised 2024-05-15, ordinance apparently 5902) now says off-street parking is not required by the Development Code; provided parking has recommended standards. Effective date not found.

Ordinance 23-2022 (signed 13 June 2022, effective on adoption) repealed the old Table 4.10-B minimums (incl. 2 spaces per dwelling) and replaced them with Market Based Vehicle Parking. Parking counts are set case by case in Plan Commission review, which is discretionary, so this may be weaker than by right.
Ordinance 1486-24 (PTA/PMA 24-0002), heard and adopted by Council 2024-06-10, repeals minimum parking requirements citywide to comply with CFEC. Effective date not stated in sources seen.
Ordinance 1754 (CDC-24-01) dated 2024-11-12 in the city ordinance table removes all parking mandates; Metro's 2024 report confirms West Linn removed all mandates.

Table 405.16.C.1 shows no residential minimum in transect zones but 1 space/unit in several special districts (including SD-MF). The repeal came bundled with a full new form-based code. Mayor signed it 2023-08-02; formal effective (filing) date not confirmed.
Ordinance 2243 adopted 2024-05-21 amended Ch. 19.600 so Table 19.605.1 lists only maximums; Metro's 2024 report confirms minimums were eliminated citywide.
Ordinance 3229 (second reading and adoption 2023-12-19) rewrote Ch. 18.4.3 so parking is voluntary with maximums only; DLCD confirmed Ashland repealed mandates citywide. Effective date not found.

The city adopted a character-based zoning ordinance effective Feb 21, 2018, and the state's best-practice guide notes it has no motor-vehicle parking schedule (so no minimums). I could not open the code PDF that PRN cites (404).

Council adopted LUO text amendments on 2023-10-24 removing single-, two- and multifamily uses from minimum parking standards in all districts except WR Watershed Residential. Geographic exception keeps it short of 'at'.

Council backed removing minimums citywide in Sept 2024; staff report says the parking text amendment's readings were completed with effect 2024-11-22. PRN's 2024-11-22 is the effective date; adoption likely 2024-10-15 (Ord. 1066, number not confirmed).

DLCD (July 2023) lists Central Point among seven cities that repealed parking mandates citywide, and Sightline reports mandates were gone by June 2023. Ordinance number and date not independently confirmed beyond PRN's 2023-06-08; city charter puts ordinances in effect 30 days after enactment.

Code 120-812C(2)(a) says no minimum number of parking spaces is required unless specified elsewhere in the chapter. The May 2018 staff memo lists 'minimum parking requirements eliminated' in the downtown-plan amendments, and the section history shows orders of 5-22-2018 and 6-12-2018.

Sec. 1137.03(a), from new zoning code Ord. 2022-110 passed 2022-12-12, says no minimum parking space count is established. PRN's 2023-03-15 is just the date the city posted the code online; the code took effect on the earliest date allowed by law (exact date not found).
LDC Sec. 5.4.1 states the code eliminates minimum parking requirements and parking is market driven; only ADA and bike minimums remain. Repeal came bundled with a full code rewrite.

Under Ord. 107-2020 (passed 10-5-20) the parking table is titled 'Maximum' but the text still requires each use to provide those spaces, with deviations only at the Zoning Administrator's discretion. That works as a minimum equal to the maximum, not a by-right removal.

The UDC (updated Aug 30, 2021) shows Table 6A converted to maximums and 6.3.3 amended. I could not find the ordinance number or date of the 2021 change, and leftover 'required' wording means a staff interpretation should be confirmed.

Code 9-4.404(f) says there is no minimum number of parking spaces for any use except accessible parking. July 2019 was only a Planning Commission study session; the Commission recommended the ordinance in Feb 2020, and it went to a council public hearing (ID-2020-102) in spring 2020 (likely April). PRN's 2019-07-19 is too early, and I did not confirm the exact adoption date. Event year set to 2020: the council heard the ordinance in spring 2020 (exact date unconfirmed).

Under Ord. 2018-0030 (4-10-2018) the former minimums became maximums in Table 94-87.1, and single-family types show 'None'. The 'shall be provided in accordance with' wording leaves some ambiguity for multifamily, so I rated it near rather than at pending staff confirmation.

Town meeting 2024-05-14 passed Amendment 4 (599-97) deleting the Article X use-by-use parking schedule, effective only once the Planning Board adopted site plan parking standards (done Dec 2024). Current zoning keeps 2-space rules for manufactured housing and a leftover PRD rule, and leaves multifamily parking to Planning Board review.

The April 17, 2024 staff report says amended UDO 7.03 makes parking rates guidelines and removes off-street parking as a requirement for all development; adopted as Ordinance 1111. The council date (2024-05-16) is PRN's; ordinance text not opened.

B3 (adopted Nov 12 2019) made parking market driven with no minimums. The April 2025 B3 text and Ord. 2024-50 (adopted Jan 14 2025) now require one space per bedroom, so the repeal was reversed after about five years; the post-period must end before 2025.

Sec. 220-73 (amended by L.L. 3-2020, 11-16-2020) says there is no minimum number of spaces, but the Planning Board determines parking to meet realistic demand and larger projects must do a demand analysis. Discretionary case-by-case requirement rather than a pure by-right repeal.

Zoning ordinance (cover: adopted July 14 2020, effective July 29 2020) Sec. 6.3.2 says there are no minimum parking requirements except where specifically required; residential uses have maximums only. PRN date of Nov 4 2021 appears to be a later record date, not the adoption; municode was blocked so the 2020 adopted text was read from a 2022 mirror.

Site plan regulations list maximums with 0 minimums for commercial uses and leave unlisted uses to Planning Board discretion; the zoning ordinance has no general residential ratio but requires parking for ADUs. Could not confirm PRN's 2019-01-08 adoption date or what changed then.

A Sept 2022 staff memo proposed removing minimums in all districts (turning them into maximums), and the ordinance's amendment table shows 4.7.1 amended 2022-11-14 (effective 2022-12-14), with more 4.7.1 subsections removed 2023-09-18 (effective 2023-10-18). PRN's 2023-11-16 is the effective date of a later amendment that did not touch 4.7.1, so PRN's date looks wrong.

Ordinance cover: adopted May 4 2021, effective May 21 2021 (city notice said May 12); Sec. 6.3.2 says there are no minimum parking requirements except where specifically required. City site PDF timed out; read via 2024 mirror.
Sec. 325-19B, amended by L.L. 2-2019 on 6-18-2019, removes any minimum number of accessory off-street spaces citywide. PRN date 2019-02-01 does not match the code note (2019-06-18).
UDC Table 8.3.6 (Ord. 2023-3, 2023-06-20) gives car spaces only as maximums, with minimums only for bike and golf-cart spaces. Repeal coincided with a full code rewrite.

City project page (LU 2024-06) says the CFEC amendments mean no minimum parking spaces for new development, with a council decision set for 2024-12-18 to meet the state's 2024-12-31 deadline. Final ordinance number and effective date not confirmed.
No minimum parking anywhere in the village, including business districts; design standards only. New Development Code adopted 2016.

Table 21-6.2.3 in city amendment documents shows maximum ratios only for motor vehicles and minimums only for bicycles for residential uses; the zoning code containing it was adopted July 28 2021. Municode itself was blocked.

§3.03.060 (Ord. 210-24, 2024-01-09) says no minimum or maximum parking is required for any use. The change was made to comply with state CFEC rules. A leftover garage requirement for houses was dropped about a year later (DC 24-02).
Sec. 14.13.015 says parking is not to drive site planning, P3 parking is market driven and P5 has maximums; no minimum ratios. Adoption date taken from PRN, not confirmed in primary source.

studies.finding: 36 major projects provided 1,942 parking spaces against 2,444 under the old minimums (79%). Mixed-use projects built 47% of the old minimum; stand-alone apartment buildings built 117% of it.
studies.source: Hess and Rehler, Journal of the American Planning Association, 2021

studies.finding: 12 projects that could cut parking built a median 0.81 spaces per home; one built none. Five that list their unit mix built 67% of what the old rule required: family-size buildings nearly all of it, studio and one-bedroom buildings about half.
studies.source: State CEQA filings, coded by this project (docs/parking/LA_TOC_RESULTS.md)

studies.finding: Reported as about 18,000 fewer parking spaces over five years than the old rules required.
studies.source: Gabbe, Pierce and Clowers, Land Use Policy, 2020

studies.finding: Exempting old downtown buildings from parking helped convert them into thousands of homes.
studies.source: Manville, Journal of the American Planning Association, 2013

studies.finding: A financial model estimates about 12.5% more market-rate apartments; a model, not observed results.
studies.source: University of Denver with the Terner Center's housing simulator
